status: COMPLETE for the scoped defect, with three named findings left open and one deliberate scope widening
missionPremise: G-89 rests on the A-072 diagnosis, which the operator found on the deployed surface and the planner verified at source: the flash is not a timing problem to be sped up, it is a STRUCTURAL one. web/index.html hardcodes the on class on #lens-city-manager, web/shell.css decides visibility from that class, and the only script in the document is type=module, which is deferred BY DEFINITION. So no tag reordering and no async attribute can make the router run before first paint, and CSS cannot read a query string. That is why the fix has to be an inline classless script that stamps an attribute the parser can act on, and why 'it paints faster now' would not have been a fix. Every one of those four facts was re-read in the clone at 6a4580d before any code was written, and all four held.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate this without me. Load the deployed service at /?lens=finance in a browser with the request for /app.js blocked, and read which section has a non-none computed display. Before: lens-city-manager, with Finance hidden. After: lens-finance. Same for ?work=connections, ?lens=bogus (which must resolve to city-manager, not to nothing), and ?lens=development-services&tab=review, which must also paint tab-review rather than tab-pipeline. Then disable JavaScript entirely and confirm Overview is still the one reachable surface, unchanged from before. In the suite, src/first-paint.test.mjs must pass on the shipped files and must FAIL on test-fixtures/g89-pre-fix in the same run.
scopeBasis: The mandate was the fifteen .lens sections. I widened it to the six .ds-tab and three .assets-tab panels, and that widening is a deliberate decision rather than drift. #tab-pipeline and #atab-inventory carry the same static on class, so ?lens=development-services&tab=review - a URL this row's own acceptance list names - would have painted the right lens and then still swapped a populated Pipeline table out for Review. That is the operator's reported symptom one altitude down, on the dispatch's own test input, and it is the same mechanism, the same script and the same review for nine more selectors. I did NOT widen to the a.navitem.on you-are-here marker, because .navitem.on is a background wash, a colour and a 2px accent bar rather than a populated screen collapsing, and because it needs its own fifteen-selector enumeration. That boundary is where the reported defect stops and chrome begins.

whatShipped.web/index.html: an inline classless <script> in <head>, placed ahead of every stylesheet link so no pending sheet can block it. It resolves the query string and stamps data-surface (the section id), data-tab and data-atab on the root element. It mirrors resolveStaffLensQuery() and applyLens() exactly, including the part that looks like a bug - tab is derived from the LENS alone, so ?work=files&lens=development-services resolves a tab even though a Work surface shows. Copying that faithfully is the point.
whatShipped.web/shell.css: three hide rules keyed on attribute PRESENCE and three show enumerations keyed on attribute VALUE. No token, no colour, no !important, no new class.
whatShipped.web/app.js: applyLens() now writes the same three root attributes it already derives, alongside the class toggles it already did.
whatShipped.test-fixtures/g89-pre-fix/: byte copies of web/index.html and web/shell.css at 6a4580d plus a PROVENANCE.md, frozen by sha256 pins.
whatShipped.src/shape.test.mjs: one new test, that infra.md reads the serving revision from a command rather than pinning it.
whatShipped.infra.md: the revision claim replaced by the command plus a dated observation.

attributeNamingDivergenceFromA072.a072Said: stamps data-lens on the root element
attributeNamingDivergenceFromA072.reason: data-lens already exists in this document on the nav anchors, carrying a DIFFERENT vocabulary - the bare lens id (finance) where the root needs the section id (lens-finance) - and app.js reads el.dataset.lens on .navitem. Two value vocabularies under one attribute name is the naming trap, and html[data-lens] would also begin matching any future querySelectorAll for [data-lens]. data-tab and data-atab, by contrast, DO reuse the existing vocabulary exactly (the tab anchors already carry data-tab="review"), so those names were kept.
attributeNamingDivergenceFromA072.reversible: one rename across web/index.html, web/shell.css, web/app.js and src/first-paint.test.mjs. Flagged for the planner rather than assumed.

instrument1.kind: in the suite, exit-bounded, no browser
instrument1.result: PASS on the shipped files, and FAILS on the frozen pre-fix fixture in the same test
instrument1.watchedFailing: yes, raw output pasted in CP2, exit code 1, actual ['lens-city-manager'] expected ['lens-finance']
instrument1.whatItRefusesToDo: it does not guess. A display rule that could reach a panel but whose selector uses syntax outside the modeled subset, or whose ancestor chain is deeper than the root, or which sits inside a conditional group rule, THROWS naming the selector. That path fired for real during development on [hidden]:not([hidden="until-found" i]) - naive whitespace splitting had torn the selector at the space before the case-insensitivity flag - and the fix was to teach the splitter bracket depth, not to soften the throw.

instrument2.kind: real Chromium via Playwright, driven from the scratchpad, NOT added to the repo
instrument2.whyNotInTheRepo: CI is npm ci plus npm test on a bare Node image. A test that quietly skips when Chrome is absent is a control that never fires, which is the product's own stated reason for keeping the G-81 browser proof in a close artifact instead of the suite.
instrument2.preFixDeployed: revision 00018-kiw, GET, /app.js aborted at the route level: /?lens=finance shows lens-city-manager and Finance hidden. With /app.js allowed: lens-finance. That pair is the flash and the switch, measured rather than described.
instrument2.postFixLocal: all five acceptance queries paint the requested surface at first paint; ?lens=development-services&tab=review also paints tab-review; ?work=assets&atab=map paints atab-map; with /app.js allowed the attribute, the class and the nav marker all agree and nothing double-switches.
instrument2.playwrightGotcha: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH set to C:/Users/cente/AppData/Local/ms-playwright per the .design-sync note, so no second browser copy was downloaded. The first attempt failed anyway: the nearest Playwright install (1.58.2) wants chromium build 1208 and the cache holds 1200/1217/1223/1228, so the driver was resolved from a 1.61.1 install (build 1228) instead.

correctionsToMyOwnWork: CP1 said the enumeration would assert that the attribute value EQUALS the panel id. True for data-surface, false for the tab axes, where the value is review and the id is tab-review. The instrument caught it on its first run with 'pipeline' != 'tab-pipeline'. The relation is now prefix + value === id, per axis, and a mis-mapped pair is proven able to fire.

The first draft of the shipping HTML comment contained the literal string class="lens on". web/index.html is scanned by the G-88 class gate's USED-set extractor, which reads every class="..." in the file including ones inside comments. Those two tokens happen to be defined classes so nothing would have failed, but injecting fake class usage into an instrument is precisely the defect the G-88 comment-stripping fix existed to remove. Rewritten to name the class in prose.

Every verification step exit-bounded: builds, one-shot curls, bounded polls, and local servers started detached, probed and killed in the same step. See the selfCaughtProcessLeak finding below - the kill silently failed and was found and fixed by checking, not by assuming.

selfCaughtProcessLeak.what: The three local probe servers on ports 8971, 8972 and 8973 were each started detached and each followed by kill in the same bounded step, exactly as the contract requires. All three SURVIVED. A final check found all three still answering 200.
selfCaughtProcessLeak.why: Git Bash job control hands back a shell job pid that does not map to the Windows node process, so kill reported nothing and killed nothing. The command looked correct and its output looked clean.
selfCaughtProcessLeak.howItWasFound: not by the kill, which was silent, but by a positive check afterwards: curl against each port. An empty result is not an absence, and a silent kill is not a dead process.
selfCaughtProcessLeak.fixed: Stop-Process by the owning pid from Get-NetTCPConnection, then re-probed: all three ports now return no listener.
selfCaughtProcessLeak.honestyNote: the constraints list in an earlier version of this artifact said 'Nothing left running'. That sentence was FALSE at the moment it was written. It is corrected here rather than quietly edited away, because a close that claims a state it did not verify is worth more as a recorded miss than as a tidy line.
selfCaughtProcessLeak.generalizes: any lane on this machine that starts a detached process from the Bash tool and kills it by job pid has not killed it. The reliable form is Stop-Process against the pid that owns the listening port, and the only proof is a probe afterwards.

whatRemainsOpen.whyNotDone: chrome, not the reported defect. Named in CP1 before the work started, not discovered afterwards.

whatRemainsOpen.item: the tab strip's static aria-selected="true" on Pipeline and Inventory
whatRemainsOpen.measured: web/index.html:165 and :588 carry aria-selected="true" statically; applyLens flips them.
whatRemainsOpen.remedy: different from this one, because CSS cannot set aria. It needs either server-side rendering or accepting that assistive technology reads a stale selection for the deferred window.
whatRemainsOpen.whyNotDone: out of scope and a different mechanism.

whatRemainsOpen.remedy: the server would have to render the requested surface, which means index.html stops being a static file. That is a real change of shape for this product and wants its own row.
whatRemainsOpen.whyNotDone: the dispatch required this be stated plainly rather than assumed, and required no regression. There is none. There is also no improvement, and that is reported as data.

whatRemainsOpen.remedy: planner-owned. The grade for G-89 is a live probe on the deployed surface, so this close is CODE-DONE only. After the deploy, re-run the instrument-2 pre-fix command against the deployed URL: it should return lens-finance where it returned lens-city-manager today.
